title: Contractor Pre-Application Checklist | Genstone
metaDescription: Before you apply to Genstone's contractor network, prepare five documents: GC license, certificate of insurance, workers' comp or waiver, W-9 and mutual NDA.
lede: Review the requirements below to make sure you have the licensing, insurance, business information and supporting documentation needed to complete your Genstone contractor application. Five documents are required. Having each one current, legible and ready to upload before you start makes the application faster and avoids a back-and-forth during review.

sections.body:
Before proceeding with the application, make sure you have each of the following ready to upload:

- General contractor license
- Certificate of insurance
- Workers' compensation certificate or workers' comp waiver
- Completed current W-9
- Mutual non-disclosure agreement

One check applies to all five. The business name should match across every document. If your license is issued to an LLC, your insurance certificate names a different trade name and your W-9 is filed under your personal name, the reviewer has to sort out which entity is actually applying. Matching names, or a short explanation where they legitimately differ, keeps the review moving.

Scan or photograph each document so every page is complete and readable, with no cropped edges, glare or missing pages. PDF is generally the easiest format to review.

Your general contractor license shows you're authorized to perform construction work where you operate. Contractors must maintain every license required by the state and local jurisdictions where they work, and those requirements vary a great deal. Some states issue general contractor licenses at the state level. Others leave licensing to counties or cities, and some jurisdictions register contractors rather than license them. Requirements can also depend on the type and size of work.

How to get it ready:

- Upload a copy of the current license or registration, showing the license number, the licensed entity's name, the classification and the expiration date.
- If you work in more than one jurisdiction that licenses separately, include each license that applies to the markets you want to work in.
- Check the expiration date. If renewal is coming up soon, renew first so the license you upload stays current through review.
- If your jurisdiction offers an online license lookup, confirm the record there matches your document.

Remember that trades such as electrical, plumbing and HVAC are often licensed separately. Partners are responsible for having licensed trades perform that work, whether in-house or through subcontractors.

A certificate of insurance (COI) is a one-page summary from your insurance agent or carrier showing the policies you hold, the carriers, the policy numbers, the coverage limits and the effective and expiration dates. It's proof that coverage is in place, and contractors must meet Genstone's insurance requirements before being approved for the network.

How to get it ready:

- Ask your insurance agent for a current certificate. Agents issue these routinely and can usually turn one around quickly.
- Make sure the named insured matches your license and W-9.
- Confirm general liability coverage is listed, along with any other coverage you carry, such as commercial auto or umbrella.
- Check the dates. A certificate showing a policy that expires soon will need replacing almost immediately.
- If Genstone's requirements call for being listed as a certificate holder or additional insured, your agent can add that. Review the current requirements before you request the certificate so you only have to ask once.

Keep your agent's contact information handy. Approved partners will need to provide updated certificates each time policies renew.

Workers' compensation insurance covers medical costs and lost wages when employees are injured on the job. Most states require it for businesses with employees, though the rules on who must carry it, and who can be exempt, differ by state.

You'll upload one of two documents:

- A workers' compensation certificate, if you carry coverage. This is often shown on the same certificate of insurance as your liability coverage, or on a separate certificate from your workers' comp carrier. Either way, it should show the carrier, policy number and effective dates.
- A workers' comp waiver or exemption, if you don't carry coverage because you qualify for an exemption, for example as a sole proprietor with no employees. The form and process depend on your state. Some states issue an official exemption certificate, while others use an affidavit or a form you complete.

If you use subcontractors, keep in mind that uninsured subs can create workers' comp exposure for the contractor who hired them. Collecting certificates or waivers from your own subcontractors is good practice.

Form W-9 is the IRS form a business uses to give its taxpayer identification number to a company that will pay it. Genstone needs one on file to set up payments and handle year-end tax reporting.

How to get it ready:

- Download the current version of the form from the IRS website. Using an outdated revision is a common reason a W-9 gets sent back.
- Enter the legal name exactly as it appears on your tax return, and your business or trade name on the second line if it's different.
- Select the correct federal tax classification (sole proprietor, single-member LLC, partnership, corporation and so on).
- Provide the correct taxpayer identification number, either an EIN for the business or an SSN where appropriate for a sole proprietor.
- Sign and date it.

The name and number on your W-9 need to match IRS records. A mismatch can hold up payment setup, so double-check them before uploading.

A mutual non-disclosure agreement (NDA) is an agreement in which both parties commit to keeping each other's confidential information private. Genstone's clients include investors, mortgage servicers, banks, REITs and investment funds, and project files can contain property addresses, ownership details, access information for vacant properties, pricing and client names. The NDA covers how that information is handled.

How to get it ready:

- Use the agreement Genstone provides with the application materials.
- Read it through before signing so you understand what it covers.
- Sign it in the name of the business entity that's applying, matching your license and W-9, and have it signed by someone authorized to bind the business.
- Upload the complete signed copy, including every page.

In practice, this means not sharing client names, addresses, lockbox codes, scopes or pricing outside the project, and not posting identifying photos of client properties publicly.

sections.h2: Apply to join the Genstone Contractor Network
sections.body: Qualified contractors must meet applicable licensing, insurance, experience and compliance requirements. Once your five documents are ready, complete the Contractor Application and upload them. Genstone will review your information and contact you about screening and onboarding. Questions before you apply can go through the contact form, using the contractor option.
